The lightning started a fire on the ship, which expanded and wrecked one adjacent barge and burned nearby docks. The ship was nearly split in half from the lightning strike, and oil seeped into Houston Ship Channel for several hours. Firefighters combated the fire on the tanker in boats, but their efforts were hindered due to unsettled weather from Elena, as well as unsafe water to travel through. The fire caused three deaths and 13 injuries, and damage related to the incident totaled $27 million (1979 USD, $76 million 2007 USD).'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: header: January 10–11, content: It started just before midnight in Tennessee on January 10 when a large, intense 400-yard-wide (370 m) F3 tornado struck Spring Hill, injuring four.
header: January 10–11, content: The next morning, an F1 tornado moved through the Northern and Eastern New Orleans suburbs, including the town of Meraux, injuring three.
header: January 19–20, content: The next day in Georgia, a large 400-yard-wide (370 m) F2 tornado struck Ellaville, Oglethorpe, and Montezuma, injuring one.
header: January 19–20, content: Another F2 tornado then struck northwest of Danville, injuring two.

header: January 19–20, content: At the same time, a large, long‐tracked 500‐yard‐wide (460 m) F1 tornado traveled through Fort Gaines, Mullins Crossroads, Southern Dawson, and Southern Lake Blackshear, causing major damage, killing one and injuring four.
header: January 19–20, content: Another F2 tornado then moved between Perry and Woody Acres as it struck Kathleen, injuring one.
header: March 1, content: A rare F1 tornado touched down in Barbers Point Housing, Hawaii. It caused only moderate damage and no casualties.
header: March 4–5, content: The next day, a large, violent F4 tornado tore through the Southern Birmingham suburbs of Bessemer, Homewood, and Mountain Brook, Alabama, injuring 35.
header: March 4–5, content: Later, the same storm produced a narrow F1 tornado that injured three in Eastern Rock Run, Alabama.
header: March 4–5, content: ... before moving into Georgia. There, it grew to 400 yards wide and struck Southern Haney, Cave Springs, and Six Mile, injuring two more.
header: March 10–12, content: A second and even more destructive outbreak of 18 tornadoes pummeled the Southeast, killing six and injuring 38.
header: March 18–19, content: First, an F1 tornado killed two women in Becks Mills, Indiana southwest of Salem.
header: March 18–19, content: Next, an F1 tornado injured four in Devon, Kentucky just outside of Cincinnati, Ohio.
header: March 18–19, content: A strong F2 tornado injured three and caused severe damage in Northern Cleveland, Tennessee.
header: March 18–19, content: Finally, the same complex of storms dropped another F2 tornado that injured one in Northwestern Athens, Tennessee.
header: March 28, content: A second rare F1 tornado struck Kawela Bay, Hawaii after coming ashore as a waterspout, injuring one person.
header: April 17, content: A localized, but destructive outbreak of six tornadoes hit Illinois, Indiana, Missouri, and Michigan, killing two and injuring 71.
header: April 18–19, content: The previous outbreak was followed by a larger outbreak of 22 tornadoes across the Midwest and the Ohio Valley, injuring 23.
header: April 22, content: Another deadly outbreak of seven tornadoes hit the Midwest, killing one and injuring 70.

Azores: On January 15, 2016, Alex traversed the archipelago bringing heavy rain and gusty winds. Rainfall reached 4.04 in (103 mm) in Lagoa, São Miguel and 3.71 in (94 mm) in Angra do Heroísmo, Terceira, with wind gusts exceeding 50 mph on Santa Maria and peaking at 57 mph in Ponta Delgada. The storm produced minor flooding, with structural damage noted as six homes in Ponta Delgada sustaining damage and another roof destroyed, plus limited landslide impacts across the central islands.

Impact: In the city of Gonzales, water from the rapidly swelling Tinsley Creek damaged approximately 30 homes and mobile homes and washed away dozens of cars.
Impact: About 50 homes and mobile homes in Waelder were flooded after multiple branches of the Baldrige Creek overflowed their banks.
Impact: Several other dwellings in and around Leesville suffered water damage after the O'Neil Creek reached its highest level since at least 1936.
Impact: Throughout Lavaca County, more than 286 homes were damaged or destroyed, along with additional infrastructure losses.
Impact: In Shiner, many cars and 118 homes were damaged, with several homes swept away by floodwaters.

Impact: A man died on U.S. Route 441 after losing control of his vehicle.

Impact: At around 8:30 AM on September 20, a man was presumed drowned in Lake Cataouatche, southwest of New Orleans. The man had been shrimping in the lake in choppy waters caused by the storm, and dove into the water without a life vest to untangle a net from his boat's propeller. After he freed the propeller, the boat was carried away by the current in the lake, and he was last seen swimming after the boat. After the disappearance, the Coast Guard launched a search with rescue boats and search dogs but could not locate him. His body was eventually found on the morning of September 22. Captain Pat Yoes, of the St. Charles Parish Sheriff's Office, said that the storm "obviously ... played a part" in the man's death, but Lieutenant Commander William Brewer of the United States Coast Guard told the press that he did not "think it was directly storm-related."

Campgrounds were damaged at Palo Duro Canyon State Park. One cabin at the park lost its entire roof and travel trailers were flipped, including one which was destroyed. Other damage at the state park including minor damage to weaker structures, and trees were damaged as well.'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: A metal building suffered minor roof damage.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Tornado Table (EF0, N of Hart, TX, March 13): 'A brief tornado flipped an irrigation pivot and caused minor roof damage to a metal building. A Texas Tech West Texas mesonet station located north of Hart measured an 87 mph wind gust as the tornado passed nearby.'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Several outbuildings were damaged (exact count not provided).
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Tornado Table (EF0, NNE of Palo Duro Canyon to ESE of Washburn, TX, March 13): 'This tornado was on the ground simultaneously with the Palo Duro Canyon EF1 tornado for several minutes as that tornado dissipated. Power poles and several outbuildings were damaged. A semi-truck was pushed over before the tornado lifted after crossing U.S. Highway 287.'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Minor damage to homes and Clarendon College; mobile homes, recreational vehicles, and boating facilities were heavily damaged with one mobile home completely destroyed.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Tornado Table (EF2, SSW of Clarendon to NE of Howardwick, TX, March 13): 'A tornado moved into the southwest edge of Clarendon, causing minor damage to homes and to Clarendon College, with sheet metal torn off the building. Mobile homes, recreational vehicles, and boating facilities were heavily damaged. One mobile home was completely destroyed, with debris from the structure scattered. Power poles were snapped, and many trees were snapped along the path.'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Several homes and sheds were damaged, with around ten homes sustaining shingle roof damage.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Tornado Table (EF0, Clarendon, TX, March 13): 'Brief, rain-wrapped tornado damaged several homes and sheds in town. Around ten homes sustained shingle damage to roofs, and several trees were downed. This tornado occurred simultaneously with and just east of the Clarendon–Howardwick EF2 tornado.'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: One shed and the porch of a home were damaged, with two additional sheds destroyed.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Tornado Table (EF1, S of Reed, OK, March 13): 'A tornado developed near the community of Russell and moved to the north-northeast. One shed, two tractors, and the porch of a home were damaged at a farm. Two sheds were destroyed at another farm. Some debris was scattered for 1.5 mi.'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: A small grain bin was destroyed.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Tornado Table (EF2, NNW of Fowler to WNW of Ensign, KS, March 13): 'Near the start of the path, the tornado overturned a pivot irrigation sprinkler. Some ground scouring was observed in farm fields along the path.'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: In Stark County, the tornado blew out 5 windows at a house and damaged the roof of a barn. In Marshall County, a barn and a pole barn were destroyed, farm equipment was damaged, and a grain bin was blown into a field. In Bureau County, the tornado struck a farmstead before dissipating, damaging the roof of the farmhouse along with several barns and outbuildings.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: List of confirmed tornadoes - April 20, 2004: Damage details spanning Stark, Marshall, and Bureau Counties.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Multiple-vortex tornado touched down just outside Utica after the main F3 dissipated. East of town, it caused damage to 2 homes, trees, and outbuildings. Part of the roof of a house was torn off. A garage and grain bin were destroyed, and another garage lost its roof. The tornado then crossed I-80, damaging a building and flipping a semi-tractor trailer. The tornado then destroyed a machine shed and downed several power poles and trees. Two houses in this area were damaged before the tornado dissipated, with one sustaining roof damage, and the other losing most of its second story.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: List of confirmed tornadoes - April 20, 2004: Detailed damage report for the area just outside Utica.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Tornado overturned a shed and a camping trailer, and snapped several trees. A detached garage was completely destroyed.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: List of confirmed tornadoes - April 20, 2004: 'Tornado overturned a shed and a camping trailer, and snapped several trees. A detached garage was completely destroyed.'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Tornado struck an industrial complex. A wastewater treatment building was destroyed, with walls blown out and structural beams bent. There was damage to overhead doors, and an air handling unit was torn from a roof of another building. Further east, there was damage to walls and roof of an outbuilding. Antennas was blown down at the fire station on Route 6.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: List of confirmed tornadoes - April 20, 2004: Damage at an industrial complex near Minooka.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Tornado affected mainly residential areas. Extensive tree damage occurred, and structures sustained minor damage. Roofs were blown off of a few homes and garages were destroyed as well.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: List of confirmed tornadoes - April 20, 2004: Residential area damage in Joliet.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: A house had its roof torn off, and numerous trees were snapped and uprooted. An empty corrugated grain bin was pushed into a tree. The tornado continued northeast to the Cognis chemical plant where the brick wall of a building fell outward. About 200 feet of chain link fence was torn up. Several cinder block buildings were damaged or destroyed in this complex just northeast of where the fence was taken out. A nearby bus garage sustained roof damage. A barn and several sheds were destroyed as well.
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: List of confirmed tornadoes - April 20, 2004: Complex damage in the S of Kankakee area affecting residential and industrial structures.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Header: Vanuatu. Content: 'While Yali passed west of the Vanuatu Islands, it came close enough to affect the isles of Tanna and Aneityum. Tanna saw about 60–70% of its crops destroyed and about 30% of its homes damaged by the storm. In Banana, vegetables and manioc crops, as well as fruit trees were entirely destroyed. In the atoll island of Aniwa, minor damage to houses and agriculture has been reported. Other places in Vanuatu only received minor damage, though Yali caused heavy rainfall and flooding throughout the island group and affected residents in low-lying areas and close to river banks.'

Header: New Caledonia. Content: 'Cyclone Yali passed just to the south of New Caledonia during March 23 and affected the Loyalty Islands, the Isle of Pines and the southern half of Grande Terre. On the Isle of Pines a rainfall total of 137 mm and a peak wind gust of 126 km/h were recorded, while some damage (torn roofs and uprooted trees) was reported in Mare, Yate and the Isle of Pines.'

Header: New Zealand. Content: 'Upon striking New Zealand as an extratropical storm, Yali caused high seas and flooding over parts of the South Island, notably around Westport and Nelson. In New Plymouth a fatality occurred and damage such as toppled trees, ripped roofs, and fallen power lines was reported. Additional impacts included road closures, air travel difficulties in Wellington due to a flying billboard, and other localized effects in Waikato, Tararuas, Picton, Hataitai, Paraparaumu, and Waikanae.'

Main_Event_Annotation: The header 'Cyclone Yali' and the opening sentence ('Severe Tropical Cyclone Yali was one of seven severe tropical cyclones...') indicate that the event is a tropical cyclone.
